──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n182\t\n183\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n184\t///\n185\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n186\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n187\tpub enum Outcome {\n188\t    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n189\t    Success,\n190\t    /// code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n199\t    Crash(i32),\n200\t}\n201\t\n202\timpl Outcome {\n203\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n204\t    ///\n205\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n206\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n207\t    ///\n208\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n209\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n210\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n211\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n212\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n213\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n214\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n215\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n216\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n217\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n218\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n219\t        if was_interrupted {\n220\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n221\t        }\n222\t\n223\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n224\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n225\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n226\t        match exit_code {\n227\t            // Success\n228\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n229\t            // Explicit failure code\n230\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n231\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n232\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n233\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n234\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n235\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n236\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n237\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n238\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n239\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n240\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n241\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n242\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n243\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n244\t        }\n245\t    }\n246\t\n247\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n248\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n249\t        match self {\n250\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n251\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n252\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n253\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n254\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n255\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n256\t        }\n257\t    }\n258\t}\n259\t\n260\t// — register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── FileSink ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Writes JSONL telemetry to `<log_dir>/<worker>-<session>.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Append-only, one line per event. The log directory is created if it\n/// does not exist.\npub struct FileSink {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    writer: std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n}\n\nimpl FileSink {\n    /// Construct a sink using the default log directory (`~/.needle/logs/`).\n    pub fn new(worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n        let log_dir = PathBuf::from(&home).join(\".needle\").join(\"logs\");\n        Self::with_dir(&log_dir, worker_id, session_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Construct a sink writing to a specific directory.\n    ///\n    /// Creates the directory (and parents) if it does not exist.\n    pub fn with_dir(log_dir: &Path, worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(log_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n        let filename = format!(\"{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl\");\n        let path = log_dir.join(filename);\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(FileSink {\n            path,\n            writer: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::io::BufWriter::new(file)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Return the path to the log file.\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file, bypassing the normal channel.\n    ///\n    /// This is called immediately after FileSink creation to ensure that even if\n    /// the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL file.\n    /// The event is written synchronously and flushed to disk.\n    fn write_boot_event_direct(\n        &self,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        Self::write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n            &self.writer,\n            &self.path,\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            version,\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), // 5 second timeout\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file with a timeout.\n    ///\n    /// This is a timeout-aware variant that prevents indefinite blocking on hung\n    /// filesystems (e.g., network filesystem issues, stale NFS mounts). If the\n    /// write takes longer than the timeout, it returns an error and the caller\n    /// can decide whether to continue or fail.\n    ///\n    /// The timeout is implemented by spawning a thread to do the blocking I/O\n    /// and joining with a timeout. If the timeout expires, the thread is detached\n    /// and will continue running (and eventually complete or be killed by the OS).\n    fn write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n        _writer: &std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n        path: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n        timeout: std::time::Duration,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::sync::mpsc;\n        use std::thread;\n\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: \"worker.booting\".to_string(),\n            worker_id: worker_id.to_string(),\n            session_id: session_id.to_string(),\n            sequence: 0,\n            bead_id: None,\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: None,\n            data: serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_id, \"version\": version }),\n            trace_id: None,\n            span_id: None,\n        };\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(&event)?;\n        let path_for_error = path.display().to_string();\n        let path_clone = path.to_path_buf();\n\n        // JoinHandle::join() has no timeout in Rust's std — use a channel with recv_timeout.\n        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Result<(), String>>();\n\n        // The JoinHandle is intentionally dropped on timeout: dropping detaches the thread,\n        // which continues running until it completes or the process exits.\n        let _handle = thread::spawn(move || {\n            let result: Result<(), String> = (|| {\n                let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                    .create(true)\n                    .append(true)\n                    .open(&path_clone)\n                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);\n                writeln!(writer, \"{line}\").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.get_ref().sync_all().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                Ok(())\n            })();\n            // Ignore send error: receiver may have timed out and been dropped.\n            let _ = tx.send(result);\n        });\n\n        match rx.recv_timeout(timeout) {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"failed to write boot event to {}: {}\",\n                path_for_error,\n                e\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"timed out writing boot event to {} after {:?} (filesystem may be hung)\",\n                path_for_error,\n                timeout\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"boot event writer thread disconnected for {}\",\n                path_for_error\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for FileSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(event)?;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writeln!(writer, \"{line}\")?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        // fsync to ensure durability before shutdown\n        writer.get_ref().sync_all()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── StdoutSink ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for interactive monitoring.\n///\n/// Format: `HH:MM:SS [worker] EVENT detail`\npub struct StdoutSink {\n    format: StdoutFormat,\n    use_color: bool,\n}\n\nimpl StdoutSink {\n    /// Create a new stdout sink from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &StdoutSinkConfig) -> Self {\n        let use_color = match config.color {\n            ColorMode::Always => true,\n            ColorMode::Never => false,\n            ColorMode::Auto => atty_stdout(),\n        };\n        StdoutSink {\n            format: config.format,\n            use_color,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format a single event as a human-readable line.\n    pub fn format_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let time = event.timestamp.format(\"%H:%M:%S\");\n        let worker = &event.worker_id;\n        let etype = &event.event_type;\n\n        // Build the summary portion based on event type.\n        let summary = self.event_summary(event);\n\n        match self.format {\n            StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Normal => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" ({summary})\")\n                };\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{summary_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Verbose => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && event.data.as_object().map_or(true, |m| m.is_empty())\n                {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" {}\", event.data)\n                };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{dur}{data_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n            \"worker.errored\" => \"ERROR\",\n            \"worker.exhausted\" => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            \"worker.idle\" => \"IDLE\",\n            \"worker.state_transition\" => \"STATE\",\n            \"worker.queue_empty\" => \"QUEUE_EMPTY\",\n            \"strand.evaluated\" => \"STRAND\",\n            \"strand.skipped\" => \"STRAND_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => \"CLAIMING\",\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => \"CLAIMED\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost\" => \"RACE_LOST\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\" => \"RACE_LOST_SKIP\",\n down `list_all()` for every workspace it appeared in, which broke\n1032\t    /// Weave/Mend/Unravel/Knot (all of which need the full bead list) on\n1033\t    /// every single cycle. json.trim();\n1039\t        if trimmed.is_empty() {\n1040\t            return Ok(vec![]);\n1041\t        }\n1042\t        // Try JSON array first (bf show returns [...])\n1043\t        if trimmed.starts_with('[') {\n1044\t            return serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(trimmed)\n1045\t                .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{json}\"));\n1046\t        }\n1047\t        // Fall back to NDJSON (bf list returns one object per line)\n1048\t        let mut beads = Vec::new();\n1049\t        for line in trimmed.lines() {\n1050\t            let line Ok(bead) => beads.push(bead),\n1056\t                Err(e) => {\n1057\t                    tracing::error!(\n1058\t                        context = %context,\n1059\t                        error = %e,\n1060\t                        line = %line,\n1061\t                        \"NDJSON parse error on one record — skipping this bead, \\\n1062\t                         keeping the rest of the list intact\"\n1063\t                    );\n1064\t                }\n1065\t            }\n1066\t        }\n1067\t        Ok(beads)\n1068\t    }\n1069\t\n1070\t    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"reopen\", id_str])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br reopen {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        // Read labels from br show --json since br doesn't have a label list subcommand.\n        // Note: v1 omitted labels here; this bead requires explicit label fetching.\n        let bead = self.show(id).await?;\n        Ok(bead.labels)\n    }\n\n    async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"label\", \"add\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br label add {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"label\", \"remove\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br label remove {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str, labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId> {\n        let mut args: Vec<String> = vec![\n            \"create\".into(),\n            \"--title\".into(),\n            title.into(),\n            \"--body\".into(),\n            body.into(),\n            \"--json\".into(),\n            \"--silent\".into(),\n        ];\n        if !labels.is_empty() {\n            args.push(\"--labels\".into());\n            args.push(labels.join(\",\"));\n        }\n        let arg_refs: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        let stdout = self.run_br(&arg_refs).await.context(\"br create failed\")?;\n        let id_str = stdout.trim();\n        if id_str.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"br create --silent returned empty ID\");\n        }\n        Ok(BeadId::from(id_str))\n    }\n\n    async fn add_dependency(&self, blocker_id: &BeadId, blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        // blocker_id blocks blocked_id (child blocks parent)\n        // br dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> --type blocks\n        // ISSUE depends on DEPENDS_ON, so blocked_id depends on blocker_id\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"dep\", \"add\", blocked, blocker, \"--type\", \"blocks\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br dep add {blocked} {blocker} --type blocks failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        // Remove the dependency: blocked_id depends on blocker_id\n        // br dep remove <ISSUE> <DEPENDENCY>\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"dep\", \"remove\", blocked, blocker])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br dep remove {blocked} {blocker} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_br(&[\"doctor\", \"--repair\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br doctor --repair failed\")?;\n        Ok(Self::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_br(&[\"doctor\"]).await.context(\"br doctor failed\")?;\n        Ok(Self::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let db_path = self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n\n        // Step 1: Remove the corrupt SQLite database.\n        if db_path.exists() {\n            tokio::fs::remove_file(&db_path)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove {}\", db_path.display()))?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %db_path.display(), \"removed corrupt database file\");\n        }\n\n        // Also remove WAL and SHM files if present.\n        for suffix in &[\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n            let wal_path = self.workspace.join(format!(\".beads/beads.db{suffix}\"));\n            if wal_path.exists() {\n                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(&wal_path).await;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Reimport from JSONL.\n        self.run_br(&[\"sync\", \"--import-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br sync --import-only failed during full rebuild\")?;\n\n        // Step 3: Verify with br doctor.\n        let verify = self\n            .run_br(&[\"doctor\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br doctor verification failed after rebuild\")?;\n        let report = Self::parse_doctor_output(&verify);\n\n        if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                report.warnings\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL — verified clean\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Use bf claim's atomic select-score-update to eliminate TOCTOU race.\n        // bf claim performs scoring (downstream_impact + critical_float + priority)\n        // and the UPDATE in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing\n        // that concurrent workers receive distinct beads.\n        match self.run_bf_claim(actor).await {\n            Ok(stdout) => {\n                // bf claim returns JSON with bead_id or empty object for no candidates\n                let trimmed = stdout.trim();\n                if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed == \"{}\" || trimmed == \"null\" {\n                    return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                }\n\n                // Parse the JSON response from bf claim\n                #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\n                struct BfClaimResponse {\n                    bead_id: Option<String>,\n                    #[allow(dead_code)]\n                    assignee: Option<String>,\n                }\n\n                let response: BfClaimResponse = serde_json::from_str(trimmed)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {}\", trimmed))?;\n\n                if let Some(bead_id) = response.bead_id {\n                    // Fetch the full bead details\n                    self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id))\n                        .await\n                        .map(ClaimResult::Claimed)\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // If bf is not available, fall back to the old br-style pattern\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"bf claim failed, falling back to br-style ready+claim\");\n                let filters = Filters::default();\n                let candidates = self.ready(&filters).await?;\n                if let Some(bead) = candidates.first() {\n                    self.claim(&bead.id, actor).await\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BrCliBeadStore {\n    /// Parse `br doctor` output into a `RepairReport`.\n    fn parse_doctor_output(stdout: &str) -> RepairReport {\n        let mut report = RepairReport::default();\n        for line in stdout.lines() {\n            if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"WARN \") {\n                // Filter out non-actionable warnings that cannot be repaired\n                // (e.g., sqlite3 binary not installed on the system, or\n                // leftover recovery backup files from a prior repair/rebuild).\n                if rest.contains(\"sqlite3 not available\") || rest.contains(\"recovery_artifacts\") {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                report.warnings.push(rest.to_string());\n            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"FIXED \") {\n                report.fixed.push(rest.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        report\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt database recovery: try repair first, then full rebuild.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the outcome of the recovery attempt. This is the primary\n    /// entry point for auto-recovery from SQLite corruption.\n    pub async fn recover_db(&self) -> RecoveryOutcome {\n        // Step 1: Try br doctor --repair.\n        tracing::warn!(\"attempting database recovery via br doctor --repair\");\n        match self.doctor_repair().await {\n            Ok(report) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    warnings = report.warnings.len(),\n                    fixed = report.fixed.len(),\n                    \"br doctor --repair completed\"\n                );\n                return RecoveryOutcome::Repaired(report);\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"br doctor --repair failed, attempting full rebuild\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Full rebuild — rm db + br sync --import + verify.\n        match self.full_rebuild().await {\n            Ok(()) => RecoveryOutcome::Rebuilt,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::error!(error = %e, \"full database rebuild failed — JSONL may be corrupt\");\n                RecoveryOutcome::Failed(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── BfCliBeadStore ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `bf` CLI-backed bead store implementation.\n///\n/// Uses `bf claim` for atomic server-selected bead claiming. This eliminates\n/// the race condition in `BrCliBeadStore.claim()` where two workers could both\n/// see the same bead in `ready()` and race to claim it.\n///\n/// The key difference: `bf claim` atomically selects AND claims a bead in a\n/// single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing that concurrent workers\n/// receive distinct beads.\npub struct BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Path to the `bf` binary.\n    pub bf_path: PathBuf,\n    /// Workspace root (directory containing `.beads/`).\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Model name for telemetry (e.g., \"claude-opus-4-7\").\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness name for telemetry (e.g., \"needle\").\n    pub harness: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness version for telemetry.\n    pub harness_version: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Construct a new store, validating that the `bf` binary exists.\n    pub fn new(\n        bf_path: PathBuf,\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        if !bf_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\"bf binary not found at {}\", bf_path.display());\n        }\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Try to find `bf` on PATH or the default install location.\n    pub fn discover(\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        let bf_path = which::which(\"bf\")\n            .or_else(|_| {\n                let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n                let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/bf\"));\n                if candidate.exists() {\n                    Ok(candidate)\n                } else {\n                    Err(anyhow!(\"bf not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/bf\"))\n                }\n            })\n            .context(\"bf CLI not found; install bead-forge\")?;\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Default timeout for bf subprocess calls (30 seconds).\n    const DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;\n\n    /// Run a `bf` subcommand in the workspace directory and return stdout.\n    async fn run_bf(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_bf_in(&self.workspace, args, Self::DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_bf_in(&self, dir: &Path, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);\n\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.bf_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn bf subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"bf subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"bf subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\"bf subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"bf stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            bail!(\"bf {args:?} exited with code {code}\\nstderr: {stderr}\\nstdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a JSON array of beads from bf output.\n    /// Handles both JSON array format `[{...},{...}]` and NDJSON (one object per line).\n    ///\n    /// A single unparseable NDJSON line (e.g. a bead carrying a status value\n    /// this build of NEEDLE doesn't yet recognize) is logged loudly and\n    /// skipped rather than failing the entire list — one bad record used to\n    /// take down `list_all()` for every workspace it appeared in, which broke\n    /// Weave/Mend/Unravel/Knot (all of which need the full bead list) on\n    /// every single cycle. This is NOT the same \"silently treat as empty\" v1\n    /// bug the module doc warns about: that bug swallowed failures and\n    /// returned nothing; this still surfaces every bad record via a loud\n    /// warning, it just doesn't discard the records that DID parse.\n    fn parse_beads(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let trimmed = json.trim();\n        if trimmed.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(vec![]);\n        }\n        // Try JSON array first (bf show returns [...])\n        if trimmed.starts_with('[') {\n            return serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(trimmed)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{json}\"));\n        }\n        // Fall back to NDJSON (bf list returns one object per line)\n        let mut beads = Vec::new();\n        for line in trimmed.lines() {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if line.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            match serde_json::from_str::<Bead>(line) {\n                Ok(bead) => beads.push(bead),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        context = %context,\n                        error = %e,\n                        line = %line,\n                        \"NDJSON parse error on one record — skipping this bead, \\\n                         keeping the rest of the list intact\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array (first element).\n    fn parse_single_bead(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let beads = Self::parse_beads(json, context)?;\n        beads\n            .into_iter()\n            .next()\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"{context} returned empty array\"))\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl BeadStore for BfCliBeadStore {\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"list\", \"--json\", \"--limit\", \"0\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf list --json failed\")?;\n        Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")\n    }\n\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let mut args = vec![\"list\", \"--json\", \"--status\", \"open\", \"--limit\", \"0\"];\n\n        // Build filter args — stored so they live long enough for the slice.\n        let assignee_arg;\n        if let Some(ref assignee) = filters.assignee {\n            args.push(\"--assignee\");\n            assignee_arg = assignee.clone();\n            args.push(&assignee_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf list failed\")?;\n        let mut beads = Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")?;\n\n        // Apply label exclusion filter (bf CLI doesn't support this natively).\n        if !filters.exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            beads.retain(|b| !b.labels.iter().any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l)));\n        }\n\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"show\", id_str, \"--json\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf show {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Self::parse_single_bead(&stdout, &format!(\"bf show {id_str} --json\"))\n    }\n\n    async fn claim(&self, _id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // BfCliBeadStore uses atomic claim_auto() for all claim operations.\n        // This eliminates the race condition from the old br-style\n        // \"update + show verify\" pattern — two workers racing to claim\n        // the same bead will always receive distinct beads.\n        self.claim_auto(actor).await\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Build bf claim args\n        let mut args = vec![\"claim\", \"--assignee\", actor, \"--json\"];\n\n        // Optional telemetry args\n        let model_arg;\n        let harness_arg;\n        let harness_version_arg;\n\n        if let Some(ref model) = self.model {\n            args.push(\"--model\");\n            model_arg = model.as_str();\n            args.push(model_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness) = self.harness {\n            args.push(\"--harness\");\n            harness_arg = harness.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness_version) = self.harness_version {\n            args.push(\"--harness-version\");\n            harness_version_arg = harness_version.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_version_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf claim failed\")?;\n\n        // Parse JSON output: {\"bead_id\": \"...\", \"reclaimed\": 0, \"assignee\": \"...\"}\n        let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {stdout}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(bead_id) = json.get(\"bead_id\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            if bead_id.is_empty() || stdout.contains(\"No beads available\") {\n                return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                    reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            // Fetch the full bead details\n            let bead = self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id)).await?;\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n        } else {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"update\", id_str, \"--status\", \"open\", \"--assignee\", \"\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf release {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        self.run_bf(&[\"sync\", \"--flush-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf sync --flush-only failed\")?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf label remove {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str,          .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep add {blocked} {blocker} --type blocks failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep remove {blocked} {blocker} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout Ok(BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let db_path = self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n\n        if ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn filters_default_is_empty() {\n        let f = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Where a configuration value originated.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ConfigSource {\n    /// Built-in default value.\n    Default,\n    /// Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`).\n    GlobalFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`).\n    WorkspaceFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Environment variable override.\n    EnvVar(String),\n    /// CLI argument override.\n    CliOverride,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ConfigSource::Default => write!(f, \"built-in default\"),\n            ConfigSource::GlobalFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::EnvVar(name) => write!(f, \"{} env var\", name),\n            ConfigSource::CliOverride => write!(f, \"CLI argument\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map of config field paths to their source.\n///\n/// Used by `needle config --dump --show-source` to annotate each value.\npub type SourceMap = BTreeMap<String, ConfigSource>;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Workspace Overrides\n// resolved NEEDLE configuration.\n///\n/// Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Config {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub #[serde(default)]\n    pub telemetry: TelemetryConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub prompt: PromptConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub health: HealthConfig,\n    /// Provider/model concurrency and rate limits.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub limits: LimitsConfig,\n    /// Per-model token pricing (USD per million tokens).\n    #[serde(default = \"crate::cost::default_pricing\")]\n    pub pricing: PricingConfig,\n    /// Daily budget thresholds for cost enforcement.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub budget: BudgetConfig,\n    /// Verification commands run after agent success, before accepting closure.\n    /// Legacy format — prefer `gates` for new configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub verification: Vec<String>,\n    /// Pluggable validation gates.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub gates: Vec<GateConfig>,\n    /// Self-modification (hot-reload) configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub self_modification: SelfModificationConfig,\n    /// FABRIC live dashboard forwarding.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub fabric: FabricConfig,\n    /// Supervisor detection configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub supervisor: SupervisorConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Config {\n    /// Expand all tilde (~) paths to absolute paths using $HOME.\n    ///\n    /// This must be called after deserialization to ensure all paths\n    /// like `~/.needle` are expanded to `/home/user/.needle`.\n    /// Paths without tildes are left unchanged.\n    pub fn expand_tildes(&mut self) {\n        // workspace section\n        self.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.default);\n        self.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.home);\n\n        // agent section\n        self.agent.adapters_dir = expand_tilde(&self.agent.adapters_dir);\n\n        // strands.explore section\n        self.strands.explore.workspace_root = expand_tilde(&self.strands.explore.workspace_root);\n        self.strands.explore.workspaces = expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.explore.workspaces);\n\n        // strands.weave section\n        self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces =\n            expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces);\n\n        // strands.splice section\n        self.strands.splice.report_workspace =\n            expand_tilde_option(&self.strands.splice.report_workspace);\n\n        // strands.pulse.scanners[].command paths are strings, not PathBuf, so skip\n\n        // strands.reflect section - no PathBuf fields\n\n        // strands.learning section\n        self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file =\n            expand_tilde(&self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file);\n\n        // telemetry section\n        if let Some(ref mut log_dir) = self.telemetry.file_sink.log_dir {\n            *log_dir = expand_tilde(log_dir);\n        }\n\n        // health section\n        self.health.heartbeat_dir = expand_tilde_option(&self.health.heartbeat_dir);\n\n        // supervisor section\n        self.supervisor.heartbeat_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.heartbeat_path);\n        self.supervisor.socket_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.socket_path);\n\n        // prompt section\n        self.prompt.context_files = expand_tilde_vec(&self.prompt.context_files);\n\n        // self_modification section\n        self.self_modification.canary_workspace =\n            expand_tilde(&self.self_modification.canary_workspace);\n\n        // prompt.variants[].content_file\n        for variants in self.prompt.variants.values_mut() {\n            for variant in variants {\n                variant.content_file = expand_tilde(&variant.content_file);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Config validation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single config validation error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ConfigError {\n    /// Dot-separated field path (e.g., `agent.default`).\n    pub field: String,\n    /// Human-readable explanation.\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, \"{}: {}\", self.field, self.message)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CLI overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// CLI-level overrides applied after all file-based config loading.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CliOverrides {\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    pub worker_name: Option<String>,\n    pub agent_binary: Option<String>,\n    pub max_workers: Option<u32>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ConfigLoader\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Loads and validates NEEDLE configuration.\npub struct ConfigLoader;\n\nimpl ConfigLoader {\n    /// Load global config from `~/.config/needle/config.yaml`.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config (not an error).\n    pub fn load_global() -> Result<Config> {\n        let path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        Self::load_from_path(&path)\n    }\n\n    /// Load config from a specific path.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config.\n    pub fn load_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Config> {\n        if !path.exists() {\n            let mut config = Config::default();\n            config.expand_tildes();\n            return Ok(config);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        let mut config: Config = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        config.expand_tildes();\n        Ok(config)\n    }\n\n    /// Load workspace overrides from `.needle.yaml` in the given workspace root.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the file does not exist. Emits warnings for\n    /// non-overridable keys found in the workspace config.\n    pub fn load_workspace(workspace_root: &Path) -> Result<Option<WorkspaceOverrides>> {\n        let path = workspace_root.join(\".needle.yaml\");\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        // Check for non-overridable keys and warn.\n        Self::warn_non_overridable_keys(&text, &path)?;\n\n        let overrides: WorkspaceOverrides = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(Some(overrides))\n    }\n\n    /// Warn about non-overridable top-level keys in workspace config YAML.\n    fn warn_non_overridable_keys(yaml_text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n        let value: serde_yaml::Value = serde_yaml::from_str(yaml_text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in workspace config: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n        if let serde_yaml::Value::Mapping(map) = value {\n            for key in map.keys() {\n                if let serde_yaml::Value::String(key_str) = key {\n                    if NON_OVERRIDABLE_KEYS.contains(&key_str.as_str()) {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            key = %key_str,\n                            path = %path.display(),\n                            \"workspace config contains non-overridable setting '{}' — ignored\",\n                            key_str,\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Apply workspace overrides to a config.\n    ///\n    /// Only overridable fields are applied. Records sources in the source map.\n    pub fn apply_workspace(\n        config: &mut Config,\n        overrides: &WorkspaceOverrides,\n        ws_path: &Path,\n        sources: &mut SourceMap,\n    ) {\n        let source = ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(ws_path.join(\".needle.yaml\"));\n\n        if let Some(ref agent) = overrides.agent {\n            if let Some(ref default) = agent.default {\n                config.agent.default = default.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"agent.default\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(timeout) = agent.timeout {\n                config.agent.timeout = timeout;\n                sources.insert(\"agent.timeout\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref routing) = agent.routing {\n                config.agent.routing = Some(routing.clone());\n                sources.insert(\"agent.routing\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref strands) = overrides.strands {\n            if let Some(ref weave_val) = strands.weave {\n                if let Ok(weave_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<WeaveConfig>(weave_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.weave = weave_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.weave\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref pulse_val) = strands.pulse {\n                if let Ok(pulse_cfg) = serde_yaml::from_value::<PulseConfig>(pulse_val.clone()) {\n                    config.strands.pulse = pulse_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.pulse\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n            if let Some(ref unravel_val) = strands.unravel {\n                if let Ok(unravel_cfg) =\n                    serde_yaml::from_value::<UnravelConfig>(unravel_val.clone())\n                {\n                    config.strands.unravel = unravel_cfg;\n                }\n                sources.insert(\"strands.unravel\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref prompt) = overrides.prompt {\n            config.prompt = prompt.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.context_files\".to_string(), source.clone());\n            sources.insert(\"prompt.instructions\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref verification) = overrides.verification {\n            config.verification = verification.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"verification\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref gates) = overrides.gates {\n            config.gates = gates.clone();\n            sources.insert(\"gates\".to_string(), source.clone());\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref ws) = overrides.workspace {\n            if !ws.labels.is_empty() {\n                config.workspace.labels = ws.labels.clone();\n                sources.insert(\"workspace.labels\".to_string(), source);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply environment variable overrides (`NEEDLE_*` prefix, `__` separator).\n    ///\n    /// Example: `NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT=opus` sets `agent.default` to `\"opus\"`.\n    pub fn apply_env_overrides(config: &mut Config, sources: &mut SourceMap) {\n        for (key, value) in std::env::vars() {\n            if let Some(suffix) = key.strip_prefix(\"NEEDLE_\") {\n                let config_path = suffix.to_lowercase().replace(\"__\", \".\");\n                let source = ConfigSource::EnvVar(key.clone());\n\n                match config_path.as_str() {\n                    \"agent.default\" => {\n                        config.agent.default = value;\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"agent.timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.agent.timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for agent.timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"agent.routing.default_adapter\" => {\n                        config\n                            .agent\n                            .routing\n                            .get_or_insert_with(RoutingConfig::default)\n                            .default_adapter = Some(value);\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"worker.max_workers\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u32>() {\n                            config.worker.max_workers = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.max_workers — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.idle_timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.idle_timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.idle_timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"worker.launch_stagger_seconds\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for worker.launch_stagger_seconds — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_interval_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for health.heartbeat_ttl_secs — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.enabled\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<bool>() {\n                            config.self_modification.enabled = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.enabled — expected true/false\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.auto_promote\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<bool>() {\n                            config.self_modification.auto_promote = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.auto_promote — expected true/false\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"self_modification.canary_timeout\" => {\n                        if let Ok(v) = value.parse::<u64>() {\n                            config.self_modification.canary_timeout = v;\n                            sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                        } else {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                env_var = %key,\n                                value = %value,\n                                \"invalid value for self_modification.canary_timeout — expected integer\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"supervisor.heartbeat_path\" => {\n                        config.supervisor.heartbeat_path =\n                            Some(expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value)));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"supervisor.socket_path\" => {\n                        config.supervisor.socket_path = Some(expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value)));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"workspace.home\" => {\n                        config.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    \"workspace.default\" => {\n                        config.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&PathBuf::from(value));\n                        sources.insert(config_path, source);\n                    }\n                    _ => {\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            env_var = %key,\n                            config_path = %config_path,\n                            \"unrecognized NEEDLE_ environment variable — ignored\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Apply CLI overrides (highest precedence) to a loaded config.\n    pub fn apply_overrides(config: &mut Config, overrides: CliOverrides) {\n        Self::apply_cli_overrides(config, overrides, &mut SourceMap::new());\n    }\n\n    /// Apply CLI overrides with source tracking.\n    pub fn apply_cli_overrides(\n        config: &mut Config,\n        overrides: CliOverrides,\n        sources: &mut SourceMap,\n    ) {\n        if let Some(ws) = overrides.workspace {\n            config.workspace.default = ws;\n            sources.insert(\"workspace.default\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        if let Some(agent) = overrides.agent_binary {\n            config.agent.default = agent;\n            sources.insert(\"agent.default\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        if let Some(n) = overrides.max_workers {\n            config.worker.max_workers = n;\n            sources.insert(\"worker.max_workers\".to_string(), ConfigSource::CliOverride);\n        }\n        // worker_name is handled at the Worker level, not stored in Config\n    }\n\n    /// Load the fully resolved configuration using the complete hierarchy:\n    ///\n    /// defaults → global file → workspace `.needle.yaml` → env vars → CLI args\n    ///\n    /// Returns the resolved config and a source map showing where each value\n    /// came from. The source map only contains entries for values that were\n    /// overridden from their defaults.\n    pub fn load_resolved(workspace_root: &Path, cli: CliOverrides) -> Result<(Config, SourceMap)> {\n        let mut sources = SourceMap::new();\n\n        // Layer 1 + 2: defaults + global config.\n        let global_path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        let mut config = Self::load_from_path(&global_path)?;\n\n        // Track which fields came from global config (if file existed).\n        if global_path.exists() {\n            let source = ConfigSource::GlobalFile(global_path);\n            // Mark all top-level sections as from global.\n            for key in &[\n                \"agent.default\",\n                \"agent.timeout\",\n                \"worker.max_workers\",\n                \"worker.idle_timeout\",\n                \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\",\n                \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\",\n            ] {\n                sources.insert((*key).to_string(), source.clone());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Layer 3: workspace config.\n        if let Some(ws_overrides) = Self::load_workspace(workspace_root)? {\n            Self::apply_workspace(&mut config, &ws_overrides, workspace_root, &mut sources);\n        }\n\n        // Layer 4: environment variables.\n        Self::apply_env_overrides(&mut config, &mut sources);\n\n        // Layer 5: CLI arguments.\n        Self::apply_cli_overrides(&mut config, cli, &mut sources);\n\n        // Expand all tildes after all overrides are applied.\n        config.expand_tildes();\n\n        Ok((config, sources))\n    }\n\n    /// Validate a resolved config.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of errors (empty = valid).\n    pub fn validate(config: &Config) -> Vec<ConfigError> {\n        let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n        if config.agent.default.is_empty() {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"agent.default\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must not be empty\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.max_workers == 0 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.max_workers\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must be at least 1\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.max_workers > 50 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.max_workers\".to_string(),\n                message: format!(\n                    \"{} exceeds practical fleet limit of 50\",\n                    config.worker.max_workers\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.worker.cpu_load_warn <= 0.0 || config.worker.cpu_load_warn > 1.0 {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"worker.cpu_load_warn\".to_string(),\n                message: \"must be in range (0.0, 1.0]\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        if config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs < 3 * config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs {\n            errors.push(ConfigError {\n                field: \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\".to_string(),\n                message: format!(\n                    \"should be >= 3 * heartbeat_interval_secs ({}); detection may be unreliable\",\n                    3 * config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Validate routing regex patterns.\n        if let Some(ref routing) = config.agent.routing {\n            for (idx, rule) in routing.rules.iter().enumerate() {\n                // Validate that match_model is a valid regex.\n                if let Err(e) = regex::Regex::new(&rule.match_model) {\n                    errors.push(ConfigError {\n                        field: format!(\"agent.routing.rules[{}].match_model\", idx),\n                        message: format!(\"invalid regex pattern '{}': {}\", rule.match_model, e),\n                    });\n                }\n                // Validate that adapter is not empty.\n                if rule.adapter.is_empty() {\n                    errors.push(ConfigError {\n                        field: format!(\"agent.routing.rules[{}].adapter\", idx),\n                        message: \"must not be empty\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        errors\n    }\n\n    /// Format config values with source annotations for `--dump --show-source`.\n    pub fn dump_with_sources(config: &Config, sources: &SourceMap) -> Vec<String> {\n        let fields: Vec<(&str, String)> = vec![\n            (\"agent.default\", config.agent.default.clone()),\n            (\"agent.timeout\", config.agent.timeout.to_string()),\n            (\"worker.max_workers\", config.worker.max_workers.to_string()),\n            (\n                \"worker.idle_timeout\",\n                config.worker.idle_timeout.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"worker.launch_stagger_seconds\",\n                config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"health.heartbeat_interval_secs\",\n                config.health.heartbeat_interval_secs.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"health.heartbeat_ttl_secs\",\n                config.health.heartbeat_ttl_secs.to_string(),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"prompt.context_files\",\n                format!(\"{:?}\", config.prompt.context_files),\n            ),\n            (\n                \"prompt.instructions\",\n                config\n                    .prompt\n                    .instructions\n                    .as_deref()\n                    .unwrap_or(\"\")\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        ];\n\n        fields\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|(key, value)| {\n                let source = sources.get(key).cloned().unwrap_or(ConfigSource::Default);\n                format!(\"{}: {} (from: {})\", key, value, source)\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Resolve a path relative to the user's home directory.\nfn dirs_or_home(relative: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n        PathBuf::from(home).join(relative)\n    } else {\n        PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\").join(relative)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Expand a leading tilde (~) to the user's home directory.\n///\n/// - `~/path` → `$HOME/path`\n/// - `~` → `$HOME`\n/// - `/absolute/path` → unchanged\n/// - `relative/path` → unchanged\n///\n/// Returns the path unchanged if HOME is not set.\nfn expand_tilde(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let path_str = path.as_os_str().to_str().unwrap_or(\"\");\n\n    // Check if path starts with ~/ or is exactly ~\n    if path_str == \"~\" {\n        if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n            return PathBuf::from(home);\n        }\n    } else if let Some(rest) = path_str.strip_prefix(\"~/\") {\n        if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\"HOME\") {\n            return PathBuf::from(home).join(rest);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No tilde or HOME not set, return as-is\n    path.to_path_buf()\n}\n\n/// Expand tildes in a vector of PathBufs.\nfn expand_tilde_vec(paths: &[PathBuf]) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n    paths.iter().map(|p| expand_tilde(p)).collect()\n}\n\n/// Expand tildes in an optional PathBuf.\nfn expand_tilde_option(path: &Option<PathBuf>) -> Option<PathBuf> {\n    path.as_ref().map(|p| expand_tilde(p))\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn default_config_is_valid() {\n        let config = Config::default();\n        let errors = ConfigLoader::validate(&config);\n        assert!(\n            errors.is_empty(),\n            \"default config has validation errors: {:?}\",\n            errors\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn missing_agent_binary_fails_validation() {\n        let mut config = Config::default();\n        config.agent.default = String::new();\n        let errors = ConfigLoader::validate(&config);\n        assert!(\n            errors.iter().any(|e| e.field == \"agent.default\"),\n            \"expected agent.default error, got: {:?}\",\n            errors\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn zero_max_workers_fails_validation() {\n        let mut config = Config::default();\n        config.worker.max_workers = 0;\n        let errors = ConfigLoader::validate(&config);\n        assert!(\n            errors.iter().any(|e| e.field == \"worker.max_workers\"),\n            \"expected worker.max_workers error, got: {:?}\",\n
